reading.p: This lesson is about using media wisely as Orthodox Christians and about treasuring the time God gives us. It draws on the lessons for Week 32 (TV and the Internet) and Week 34 (The Value of Time), as well as the Orthodox Study Bible and the writings of Fr. Tadros Y. Malaty.

reading.quote: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

list: Media has power: it shapes our thoughts, habits, desires, and behavior.
Our senses are spiritual gates; what we watch, hear, and scroll can affect the heart.
Time is a gift from God: once it passes, it cannot be recovered.
Not all content is beneficial; Christians must be selective and spiritually awake.
God must receive our best time, not only what is left over.
We are called to holiness, even in how we use technology and entertainment.

reading.p: Let us be honest with ourselves. How much time do you spend each day on your phone, TV, YouTube, TikTok, games, or streaming? What kind of content do you watch most? Does your media use bring you closer to God or distract you from Him? Do you control your screen time, or does your screen time control you?
Here is a key question to consider: if someone looked at your media habits, what would they think you love most?
God calls us to guard two things together: our purity and our time.

reading.quote: You shall be holy, for I am holy.
Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

reading.p: Media itself is not the problem. The issue is how we use it and what we allow it to do to our soul. Used wisely, it can be a real blessing.

list: Learn useful information
Understand events happening in the world
Watch Christian teaching and edifying messages
Hear sermons, hymns, and spiritual reflections
Communicate with others
Grow in knowledge when used wisely

reading.p: Media becomes useful when it serves a holy and meaningful purpose.

list: Learn history, science, language, and life skills
Stay informed about important news
Access Orthodox sermons, Bible studies, and hymns
Share the faith with others
Encourage others through good messages
Use technology for school, work, ministry, and service

reading.p: What enters the eyes and ears can settle in the heart. Much content can harm the soul.

list: Sexual impurity
Violence
Dirty language
Pride and vanity
Addiction to entertainment
Jealousy and comparison
Laziness and wasted time
Distraction from prayer and spiritual life

reading.h2: The Senses Are Gates to the Soul

reading.p: Our senses are gates, and media can shape what passes through them: our thoughts, imagination, desires, language, emotions, our view of sin, and even our relationship with God.
Here is a spiritual truth to remember: if we constantly feed the flesh, the flesh becomes stronger; but if we feed the spirit, the spiritual life becomes stronger.

reading.quote: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it spring the issues of life.

reading.p: Before consuming content, ask yourself these questions:

list: Is this making my heart cleaner or darker?
Is this helping me love God more?
Is this weakening my purity?
Is this filling my mind with temptation?
Would I watch this if Christ were sitting beside me?

reading.quote: All things are lawful for me, but all things are not helpful.

reading.p: Do not only ask, "Is this allowed?" Also ask: Is this beneficial? Is this pure? Is this wise? Is this helping my salvation? Is this controlling me?

reading.h2: Time Is a Gift from God

reading.p: Every day we receive 24 hours, which is 1,440 minutes, or 86,400 seconds. But once that time passes, it is gone. Money can be regained and possessions can be replaced, but lost time cannot be brought back. Time is one of the greatest treasures God gives us.
Wasted time becomes dangerous when it replaces prayer, Scripture, service, family, study, and spiritual growth. Watch out for habits such as these:

list: Endless scrolling
Binge-watching
Gaming without limits
Watching random videos for hours
Following celebrity drama
Talking online with no purpose
Staying up late consuming useless content

reading.quote: See then that you walk circumspectly… redeeming the time.

list: Use time wisely
Do not live carelessly
Do not delay repentance
Do not waste your youth
Do not let distractions steal your spiritual life
Give God your best, not your leftovers

reading.quote: The days of our lives are seventy years; and if by reason of strength they are eighty years…

reading.p: Our life on earth is temporary. This should not make us afraid; it should make us awake. We were not created only to be entertained. We were created to know God, love God, serve God, and prepare for eternal life.

Many people say, "I do not have time to pray." Yet we often have time for social media, movies, shows, music, games, group chats, and random scrolling. The real question is not only, "Do I have time?" but rather, "What am I choosing to give my time to?"

reading.h3: Giving God the First and Best

reading.p: God should not receive only our leftover time. A spiritual person gives God priority. Set time for prayer, for Scripture and spiritual reading, and for Church, confession, repentance, service, and silence with God. If God is first in our life, He must also be first in our schedule.

reading.h2: Set Goals According to God's Will

reading.p: Spiritual maturity begins when we stop drifting and start living intentionally before God. Reflect honestly on these questions:

list: What does God want from my life?
What habits are helping me grow spiritually?
What habits are pulling me away from Him?
What should I stop?
What should I start?
What kind of person am I becoming?

reading.quote: To everything there is a season, a time for every purpose under heaven.

reading.p: There is a proper place in our lives for God, family, school or work, Church, rest, service, health, and spiritual growth.

Many people finish everything else and then give God whatever energy remains, so that by the end of the day they are too tired to pray or read Scripture. Do not give God the weakest part of your day. Give Him time when your mind is awake, your heart is attentive, and your spirit is ready.
Your screen time may reveal your spiritual priorities. At the end of a day, ask yourself:

list: How much time did I spend with God?
How much time did I spend on entertainment?
What content affected my thoughts the most?
What did I watch that I should not have watched?
What did I listen to that weakened my spirit?
What did I consume that brought me closer to God?

reading.h2: How to Avoid the Destructive Impact of Media

list: Fill your free time with God and His Word.
Set limits on entertainment and scrolling.
Be selective about what you watch and hear.
Avoid content that weakens purity.
Replace harmful content with spiritual content.
Do not browse without purpose.
Protect your heart before small sins become strong habits.

reading.p: If it weakens your soul, it is not worth your time. Run your media through this filter: Is it pure? Is it useful? Is it controlling me? Is it wasting time? Is it leading me toward sin? Is it helping me grow? Would I be comfortable bringing this before God?

reading.h2: The Orthodox Way of Using Technology

reading.p: Technology should be a servant, not a master. Use media for learning, communication, ministry, encouragement, spiritual growth, evangelism, creativity, and work. Never allow technology to rule your thoughts, to steal your peace, to pollute your senses, or to replace your relationship with God.
Take up the 7-Day Guard Your Time Challenge: reduce bad habits and replace them with holy habits.

list: Limit unnecessary screen time.
Avoid one type of content that weakens your purity.
Spend at least 10 minutes daily in prayer.
Read one passage of Scripture each day.
Replace one entertainment habit with something spiritually useful.
Track how much time you spend with God compared to media.

reading.p: So, when, where, how, and for how long will you meet with God? Do not answer this only in words. Answer it with your schedule, with your habits, and with what you choose to watch, hear, avoid, and prioritize. Today is the only day you truly have; tomorrow is not promised.

TV, the internet, and media have a powerful impact on our lives, thoughts, behavior, and spiritual condition. As Orthodox Christians, we are called to be awake, selective, pure, and wise. We must guard our senses, protect our hearts, and redeem the time God has given us. Use media without being ruled by it. Use time without wasting it. Live holy, because God is holy.

studyGuide.overview: This lesson teaches Orthodox Christians to use media wisely and to treasure time as a gift from God. Because the senses are gates to the soul, we must be selective about what we watch and hear, and because lost time cannot be recovered, we must give God our first and best time rather than our leftovers.
keyPoints: Media is not inherently bad; the issue is how we use it and what we let it do to the soul.
The senses are gates to the soul, so what we consume shapes our thoughts, desires, and relationship with God.
Feeding the flesh strengthens the flesh; feeding the spirit strengthens the spiritual life.
Time is an irreplaceable gift; money and possessions can be regained, but lost time cannot.
God deserves our first and best time, not our leftovers, and this should show in our schedule.
A Christian media filter asks not only 'Is it allowed?' but 'Is it pure, useful, and helping my salvation?'
Technology should be a servant, not a master.
reviewQuestions: Why does the lesson say the senses are 'gates to the soul'?
What is the difference between asking 'Is this allowed?' and 'Is this beneficial?' (1 Corinthians 6:12)?
Why is wasted time more dangerous than wasted money or possessions?
What does it mean to 'redeem the time' according to Ephesians 5:15-16?
Why should God receive our best time rather than our leftover time?
What is one practical change you can make this week using the 7-Day Guard Your Time Challenge?
